title: Ninajirachi Wins NSW Breakthrough Artist of the Year at 2025 ARIA Awards
text:
Ninajirachi won NSW breakthrough artist of the year at the 2025 ARIA Awards, as part of the inaugural NSW music prize recognizing local talent with A$160,000 in total awards.
Ninajirachi, Boy Soda and Keli Holiday have been shortlisted for the 2026 NSW Music Prize, the second edition of the state government initiative. Other homegrown talent shortlisted for the top prize include Don West, Esha Tewari, MAY-A, Parcels, The Rions and ZIPPORAH. The main award comes with an A$80,000 (US$55,000) winner's check.
The main award is for the NSW artist or act whose release has had the most significant impact. The NSW First Nations music prize, worth A$40,000, is awarded to the NSW-based Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander artist or act whose release has had significant and meaningful impact. The NSW breakthrough artist of the year award, also A$40,000, is for an emerging NSW artist or act who has had a groundbreaking year.
The Minns Labor government is behind the initiative, launched to help inspire the next wave of artists in NSW, which until 2025 was the only state without a dedicated music prize. A statement noted that local artists have been under increasing pressure due to cost-of-living pressures and the dominance of overseas artists on streaming platforms. This prize is designed to give them recognition and momentum.
A panel of artists and industry leaders formed the committees that identified the nominations, announced Friday, October 16. All winners will be revealed during a ceremony on November 9 at the Museum of Contemporary Art's Foundation Hall in Sydney. The main categories will be decided by a five-person judging panel, while the NSW First Nations music prize winner will be chosen by a three-strong First Nations judging panel.
John Graham, state minister for music and the night-time economy, commented, congratulating all finalists and calling the recognition a testament to their creativity and hard work. He referenced AC/DC's song, saying it is a long way to the top, and added that the prize is about helping artists stay the course and become the next big NSW icons. Graham also noted that musicians have been under so much pressure since the pandemic, and that if they are lost, the local sound is lost with them. He said the government is backing them with targeted support and celebrating them with this prize.
At the 2025 ARIA Awards, held at the Hordern Pavilion in Sydney on November 19, 2025, BARKAA collected the inaugural NSW First Nations music prize for her EP Big Tidda, and Ninajirachi won for NSW breakthrough artist of the year. The awards were presented during the ceremony, highlighting the importance of local talent.
The NSW music prize aims to provide financial support and recognition to artists in New South Wales, helping them overcome challenges and continue contributing to the state's music scene. The 2025 ARIA Awards served as the platform for presenting these inaugural awards.
